name: Jay Gupta
school: B.Tech + MBA Tech (AI), NMIMS MPSTME, Mumbai
headline: I'm Jay, an AI engineer who takes an idea from raw data to a working product, and I don't stop until the numbers are real.
intro: Recommenders, computer vision on live telescope data, reinforcement learning for portfolios, and LLM pipelines. Each project here is a working system with held-out results, not a notebook.

stats.label: held-out events in one test set

projects.title: SmartCross
projects.summary: Predicts the next financial product a bank customer will take up, and explains why.
projects.problem: Banks cross-sell blindly. On LendingClub I showed that credit data describes how much someone can borrow, not what they want, so no algorithm could fix it. The signal had to come from behaviour.
projects.built: On Santander's 17 months of product holdings I found 112,063 acquisition events and 175 sequence rules. The final system fuses four engines: collaborative peers, a gradient-boosted content model reading 3 months of holdings history, sequence rules and a macro regime. One FastAPI app serves it, with a console that pulls a real held-out customer and checks its own answer.
projects.result: 85.3% top-3 hit rate on 104,167 held-out events (95% CI 85.1 to 85.6), against 70.5% for recommending the most popular products and about 14% for random picks.

chart.caption: Top-3 hit rate on 104,167 held-out acquisition events, Mar to May 2016.

projects.note: tested on 104,167 real customers, not a demo

projects.title: Cosmic Watch AI
projects.summary: A 3D observatory that pulls live data from real telescopes and spacecraft and runs my own neural networks on it.
projects.problem: Rubin, JWST, the Sun's monitors, LIGO and the Mars rovers publish data in minutes, but each in its own format and none of it is easy to look at together.
projects.built: 13 live feeds (Rubin and ZTF alerts, JWST and Hubble, SDO, GOES, SOHO, LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA, NASA GCN, Mars rovers, JPL asteroids, ISS). Source extraction on deep fields, a sunspot and CME detector, and two CNNs I trained on an RTX 3060: a fine-tuned Zoobot ConvNeXt for galaxy shapes and a Mars terrain classifier. Six 3D worlds you can fly through, or steer with your bare hands through the webcam.
projects.result: Galaxy CNN reaches 88.7% accuracy on 10 classes (97.2% top-2), up from 82.8% for my first ResNet-18. The Mars CNN gets 80.0% top-1 and 89.0% top-3 on unseen terrain.

chart.caption: Validation on 2,656 galaxies (Galaxy10 DECaLS) and the Mars held-out split.

projects.note: you can fly it with your bare hands

projects.title: SharpeShooter
projects.summary: An RL agent sets weekly weights for 30 large US stocks. I tested, once and honestly, whether it beats splitting the money equally.
projects.problem: Most RL trading demos look great because they peek at the future or tune on the test set. I wanted an answer I could defend.
projects.built: A2C and REINFORCE written from scratch in PyTorch, reading 664 inputs a week: prices, SEC financials and 168,635 news headlines scored with FinBERT, all used only after they became public. 400 walk-forward runs picked the design; the 2022-23 holdout was opened once. A React app replays the agent's decisions and matches Python to 1e-6.
projects.result: No edge: Sharpe 0.14 against 0.19 for equal weight, with a 90% interval for the gap of -0.18 to +0.16. Sanity checks prove the learner works: on a market with a planted signal it scores 3.88.

chart.caption: Sharpe ratio on the unseen 2022-23 holdout, after 10 bp trading costs.

projects.note: yes, I published the miss. that's the point

projects.title: PulseAI
projects.summary: Reads 15 AI news sources every 30 minutes, merges duplicate coverage and sends each subscriber a personal digest by email and WhatsApp.
projects.problem: AI news repeats the same story across a dozen sites. A useful digest has to merge them, rank them for one reader and summarise without making things up.
projects.built: bge-small embeddings cluster articles into stories, with a keyword check for the grey zone a single threshold missed. Stories are ranked by recency, coverage, credibility and substance, personalised with a feedback loop and MMR, and summarised by Gemini with Groq and Ollama fallbacks. A WhatsApp agent answers questions over the archive with RAG, and only sends an answer the model marks grounded and backs with a citation. Celery, Redis, Postgres and Docker, all on free tiers.
projects.result: Duplicate detection F1 0.941 (precision 0.889, recall 1.0) and retrieval MRR 0.823 on a labelled eval that runs as a CI quality gate. First live run: 2,570 items became about 80 stories in 40 seconds on CPU.

chart.caption: Offline evaluation on a labelled set of news articles and questions.

projects.note: it won't answer unless it can cite a source

approach.title: Hold out, then open it once
approach.text: Test data stays sealed until the design is final. SharpeShooter's 2022-23 holdout was run a single time.

approach.title: Beat a simple baseline first
approach.text: Every model is compared with the dumbest thing that could work: most-popular, equal weight, a ResNet-18.

approach.title: Report the miss
approach.text: When a model does not win, the result says so, with the interval and the sanity checks that rule out a bug.

approach.title: Ship something people can run
approach.text: Trained models are committed with a version lock, so a teammate can clone and run without retraining.

coursework: Reinforcement Learning labs: TD learning, Q-learning and SARSA, linear value-function approximation, each as an executed, commented notebook.
